about: The effects layer of the 3D route (docs/3d-effects.md). HOI4 effects are not part of a model: they are particle systems fired by `event` lines in the entity's states at a locator, a named point of the .mesh that follows a bone. A profile is one effect of a unit: its slots (a locator, the spot it is measured at, the roles whose states fire it, the frame rule) and the particles each slot fires. A Tripo preset lists the profiles that fit its type (`effects` in tripo_presets.json), a job picks among them and states its setting. `needs` names what the unit's world must have for the profile to fit (D-127): a medieval or fantasy world without gunpowder can never take a muzzle flash. Particles marked `vanilla` are fired by their registered vanilla name, untouched. Particles with `from` are copied from that vanilla particle's file into the mod under the unit's own name, and changed by colour and scale only. Locator names are `<effect>_<part>`, with `_l` or `_r` by the rig's side (fire_mouth, fire_hand_l, glow_eye_r), so every type uses one scheme, except the vanilla names a static model keeps (barrel, hit_effect_locator1). lib/unit_effects.py reads this file and refuses a profile that names an unknown spot, frame rule, particle or vanilla particle (checked against effects_vanilla.json, which calibrate_effects.py writes from the game). The profiles are general, one per kind of effect, with type defaults (D-134). Which effect a mod's creature has, from its own canon, lives in that mod's job files (the job's effects block), never here.

setting_tags.gunpowder: the unit's world has firearms, cannons and explosives (HOI4's own era, a modern faction)
setting_tags.magic: the unit casts spells (a mage, a necromancer)
setting_tags.fire_creature: the unit shoots or breathes fire by its own nature (a fire demon, a dragon)

spots.locator: an existing locator of the mesh, named by `locator` (the static route's measured barrel tip, a ship's hit locators)
spots.hand_tip: the tip of a hand: the mean of the hand region's vertices farthest along the forearm-to-hand direction (the bone and its children)
spots.head_front: the front of the head or snout: the mean of the head region's vertices farthest toward the unit's front, in the lower part of the head (the mouth)
spots.eye: one eye (`side` l or r): the upper front of the head region on that side, pushed back by `inset` of the head's depth (default 0.25), so it sits inside a hood's opening and not on its rim
spots.wing_tip: a wing's tip (`side` l or r): the farthest 5% from the mid-plane of the vertices whose strongest bone is a wing bone, parented to the wing bone that carries most of them
spots.bone_top: the top centre of a bone's own part, without the parts mounted on it (a hull's deck under its turret)
spots.bone_bottom: the bottom centre of a bone's own part (a turret's ring)
spots.bone_centre: the centre of a bone's own part. A slot's `parent` hangs the locator from another bone: measured on the turret, hung from the hull, a blast stays where the turret was as it flies off
spots.box_share: a point of the model's box, as shares of its size per axis (`share`), parented to `bone` or to none

frame_rules.start: frame 0, as vanilla fires most effects. A looping particle (duration_s loop) starts here and glows all through the state
frame_rules.recoil: the first frame the gun recoils: the bone among the locator's bone and its two parents whose own translation channel moves most, at the frame it first passes 10% of that move
frame_rules.strike: the frame the locator reaches farthest toward the unit's front, measured from the unit's centre in that frame (a claw's rake, a cast's thrust, a breath's lunge, a wing's beat)
frame_rules.part_leaves: the first frame the locator has moved more than 2% of the model's height from where it was at frame 0 (a turret blown off)
frame_rules.peak: the frame the locator is farthest from where it was at frame 0 (a hand raised to cast)

tank_cannon.label: a tank's main gun: muzzle flash and gun smoke at the barrel tip when it fires
tank_cannon.vanilla: light tanks fire light_tank_attack_barrel_particle and its smoke at the barrel locator (bone barrel_tip) in attack, defend and support_attack (28 entities)

heavy_cannon.label: a heavy tank's or gun's main gun
heavy_cannon.vanilla: heavy tanks fire heavy_tank_attack_barrel_particle and its smoke at barrel (bone barrel_tip)

tank_wreck.label: a tank's death: an explosion at the turret ring as the turret blows off, then the hull burns and smokes
tank_wreck.vanilla: vanilla tanks have no death particles. Planes fire vehicle_explode_effect in their explode state and destroyed landmarks fire it at impact locators, so the wreck takes those

firearm.label: a rifle or musket: muzzle flash and smoke at the weapon's tip
firearm.vanilla: infantry weapons fire rifle_muzzle_particle (or mg_muzzle_particle) and mg_muzzle_smoke_particle at a muzzle locator of the weapon entity

ship_death.label: a ship's death: explosions at the hull's hit locators
ship_death.vanilla: ship deaths fire ship_explosion_particle at hit_effect_locator1 and 2 (bone root or none), 0 to 1.2 s apart (26 entities)

plane_crash.label: a plane's crash: an explosion at the engine
plane_crash.vanilla: plane crash states fire explosion_particle at engine1 to engine4 (bone root, 24 entities)

building_destroyed.label: a building's or landmark's destruction: timed explosions, then fire and smoke
building_destroyed.vanilla: destroyed landmarks fire ship_explosion_particle, building_explode_effect, vehicle_explode_effect and building_fire_particle at locators on root, timed over the destroy clip

hand_mouth_fire.label: fire shot from both hands and the mouth at the strike, orange-red with dark smoke
hand_mouth_fire.vanilla: no vanilla unit shoots fire from hand or mouth. The flame is vanilla's flamethrower_particle (flame tanks, at the barrel tip), recoloured orange-red, with the flame tank's own smoke

heavy_fire.label: a heavy lava-orange gout from the mouth and both hands at the attack, with near-black smoke
heavy_fire.vanilla: the flame tank's flamethrower_particle, recoloured a deeper lava orange and larger, and its smoke tinted near black

ember_idle.label: slow embers from the body while the unit stands (idle only)
ember_idle.vanilla: vanilla's sparks_effect (power line sparks), recoloured ember orange and small, kept looping

wing_gust.label: a physical wing beat: dust thrown from both wing tips at the strike, nothing glowing
wing_gust.vanilla: vanilla's dustcloud_particle as it is. Vanilla has no feather particle, and a copy may change only colour and scale, so loose feathers need a new particle (a decision, not a route step)

strike_dust.label: a heavy blow: dust and chips at both fists at the strike (a stone or earth creature)
strike_dust.vanilla: vanilla's building_damaged_particle (dust and debris of a damaged building) as it is

eye_glow.label: a constant faint glow of two eyes (in a hood or a dark face), in every state but death
eye_glow.vanilla: vanilla's map lamp (lamp_red_particle, one pulsing glow kept at its locator, local_space on), recoloured purple and small, kept looping, as vanilla's infantry keeps cigarette smoke at its head locator in idle

spell_cast.label: a spell: a coloured swirl with dark wisps from the raised casting hand at the attack (purple by default, the job sets the colour)
spell_cast.vanilla: vanilla has no spells. The swirl is the flame tank's flamethrower_particle recoloured magenta-purple and smaller, the wisps its smoke tinted dark purple

smoke_death.label: a death that unravels into coloured smoke (purple by default)
smoke_death.vanilla: vanilla's city_smoke_particle tinted purple for the length of the death, with the spell's swirl

fire_breath.label: a fire-breathing beast: a flame and its smoke from the mouth as it lunges
fire_breath.vanilla: flame tanks fire flamethrower_particle at the flamethrower locator (bone barrel_tip) at 0.1 s and flamethrower_smoke_effect at 0.2 s
